feature_engineering: None — model trains on the 41 raw daily fields the caregiver screening form actually collects.

Earlier v3 added lag1 / roll3 / delta7 / dow / dom (160 features total), but those engineered fields were never available at serve time — the live API was running on a degraded vector the model never saw during training. v4 fixes that by retraining on what the API actually has.
selection: Optuna TPE, 80 trials per algo, 3-seed × 5-fold GroupKFold-by-patient AUC averaged inside the objective.
split: GroupKFold by patient_id, mean across 3 row-permutation seeds
caveats: Class prevalence in the TIHM 1.5 cohort is ~4.2 % (114 positives in 2 722 rows). The default 0.5 threshold yields very low precision/recall by design — the model is cautious about a rare positive class. AUC and average-precision are the meaningful single-shot quality numbers.

v4 headline GroupKFold-by-patient AUC is 0.890, slightly above v3's reported 0.885 even though v4 drops all 119 engineered features. Two reasons it didn't regress: (a) v3's evaluation was single-seed; v4 averages across 3 row-permutation seeds, which both tightens the estimate and is more honest. (b) The engineered features were apparently adding less signal than v3's metric suggested.
in_sample_ap (0.993) is computed on the same data the model was trained on — it's NOT a generalisation estimate. The honest number for held-out patients is groupkfold_auc_mean (0.890).
Not a medical device. Surfaces concerning patterns to a caregiver; never replaces clinical assessment.
